title: Se déplacer et nommer les objets utiles
summary: Describe transport, distinguish travelling by from being inside a vehicle, and interpret noun groups built with `à`, `de` or `en`.
objectives: Use ordinary transport expressions and distinguish mode from physical location.
Use `dans` for streets and vehicle interiors.
Distinguish purpose, contents and material in familiar compound noun groups.

sections.title: Name the travel mode with `en` or `à`
paragraphs: Common enclosed-vehicle travel modes use `en` without an article: `en voiture`, `en train`, `en bus`, `en métro`, `en avion`. Conventional exposed modes include `à pied`, `à vélo`, `à bicyclette`, `à moto` and `à cheval`. You will also hear and read `en vélo` and `en moto`; `à vélo/à moto` are safe reference forms, not a reason to claim all `en` variants are impossible.

When describing your physical position, use the relevant location preposition plus an article: `dans le bus`, `dans la voiture`, `sur le vélo`. `En bus` describes how you travel; `dans le bus` says where you are. English on the bus normally corresponds to `dans le bus`, not being on its roof.
points: `Un train` (m.) = a train; `une voiture` (f.) = a car; `un vélo` (m.) = a bicycle.
`À pied` keeps `pied` singular in the ordinary expression.

examples.english: We go to work by train.
I am going home on foot.
I am reading on the bus.
examples.note: Physical location inside the vehicle differs from mode of transport.

mistakes.why: The transport-mode expression has no article.

sections.title: A street is normally introduced with `dans` when describing activity there
paragraphs: French usually says `marcher dans la rue`, `jouer dans la rue` or `habiter dans cette rue`. This does not mean underground inside the road; it is the normal way to place activity in the street area. A precise address can use `au` + number, followed by the street name: `au 12, rue des Lilas`. Usage with streets varies regionally, but `dans la rue` is a safe general activity expression.
points: `Une rue` (f.) = a street; `une avenue` (f.) = an avenue.

examples.english: The children are playing in the street.
examples.note: `Dans` is the normal location preposition here.
Do not translate English on mechanically as `sur`.

mistakes.why: Use `dans` with the ordinary definite street noun phrase.

sections.title: A linking preposition can identify an object's purpose, contents or material
paragraphs: French often uses noun + preposition + noun where English uses two nouns together. `À` can indicate a purpose or type: `une tasse à café` (a coffee cup), `une brosse à dents` (a toothbrush). `De` can indicate contents: `une tasse de café` (a cup of coffee), `un verre d'eau` (a glass of water). `En` often names material: `une table en bois` (a wooden table). Established expressions must be learned; do not mechanically substitute one preposition everywhere.

Noun + `à` + infinitive names a thing's intended function: `une machine à laver` (a washing machine), `une salle à manger` (a dining room), `une machine à coudre` (a sewing machine). The infinitive does not agree with the noun and is not conjugated. This identifying `à` differs from `pour` + infinitive giving the purpose of someone's action.
points: `Une tasse` (f.) = a cup; `une brosse` (f.) = a brush; `le bois` (m.) = wood; `une machine` (f.) = a machine.

examples.note: The phrase names the cup's intended type, not its contents.

examples.english: He prepares a cup of coffee.

examples.french: La **machine à laver** est dans la cuisine.
examples.english: The washing machine is in the kitchen.

examples.french: Ils mangent dans la **salle à manger**.
examples.english: They eat in the dining room.
examples.note: `Manger` remains an infinitive in the noun group.

mistakes.why: The functional noun construction uses an infinitive after `à`.

sections.title: Recognise conventional alternatives without inventing a universal `par` rule
paragraphs: `En train` and `en avion` are useful default travel-mode phrases. `Par le train` and `par avion` are also established ways of naming the means used. Notice that these two `par` phrases do not use the same article pattern. Learn the combinations rather than replacing every `en` with `par` plus a definite article.

examples.french: Nous faisons ce trajet **par le train**, pas par la route.
examples.english: We make this journey by train, not by road.
examples.note: `Par le train` is an alternative means-of-transport expression.

sections.title: A named address can omit the street preposition
paragraphs: With `habiter` and a named street, French can give the address directly: `habiter rue des Tilleuls`. `Habiter` can also take a place as its direct object: `habiter cette rue` is grammatical alongside `habiter dans cette rue`. These possibilities belong to `habiter`; they are not a reason to remove `dans` from ordinary phrases such as `jouer dans la rue`.

examples.english: My cousin lives on Rue des Tilleuls.
examples.note: The name functions as an address.

examples.french: Elle **habite dans cette rue**, près du cinéma.
examples.english: She lives on this street, near the cinema.
examples.note: `Dans` is natural here, but not obligatory after `habiter`.

examples.french: Leur famille **habite cette rue** depuis longtemps.
examples.english: Their family has lived on this street for a long time.
examples.note: `Habiter` takes `cette rue` directly as its object in this construction.

sections.title: A linking preposition does not have just one meaning
paragraphs: `À` can identify an ingredient or flavour, not only an object's purpose: a dessert `à la vanille` is vanilla-flavoured. Keep the article and the ordinary contractions, such as `au` and `aux`. Material can also use `de` in established combinations, as well as `en`. Therefore neither every `à` means for nor every `de` means filled with. Use the relation and the established noun group together.
points: `La vanille` (f.) is vanilla; `une noix` (f.) is a nut; `la pierre` (f.) is stone.

examples.french: Je prépare une crème **à la vanille**.
examples.english: I am making a vanilla custard.

examples.french: Le boulanger vend du pain **aux noix**.
Un mur **de pierre** entoure la cour; le banc est **en pierre**.
examples.english: A stone wall surrounds the courtyard; the bench is made of stone.
examples.note: `De` and `en` can both introduce material in these established combinations.

practice.prompt: Supply the article in the taught alternative: 'Les marchandises arrivent par ___ train.'
practice.explanation: Par le train uses le; do not infer that par avion needs it too.

practice.prompt: Express by air using par and avion: 'Nous expédions le paquet ___.'
practice.explanation: The established mode expression is par avion, without an article.

practice.prompt: Must 'Nous voyageons par le train' be rejected because en train is also possible?
practice.explanation: Both are established expressions for the means of travel.

practice.prompt: Is 'Il habite rue des Verriers' a possible French address construction?
practice.explanation: A named street can directly follow habiter.

practice.prompt: Supply dans or no word (write 'rien') for the ordinary demonstrative phrase: 'Elle habite ___ cette rue.'
practice.explanation: Habiter dans cette rue and transitive habiter cette rue are both grammatical; dans is not obligatory with this verb.

practice.prompt: Rewrite only by removing dans la to give the direct named-street address: 'Nous habitons dans la rue du Canal.'
practice.explanation: Rue du Canal can directly identify the address after habiter.

practice.prompt: Complete the ingredient contraction à + les: 'une brioche ___ raisins'.
practice.explanation: Aux raisins identifies an ingredient, not a purpose for the brioche.

practice.prompt: Supply à la or de la to name vanilla flavour in this taught construction: 'une crème ___ vanille'.
practice.explanation: À la vanille identifies the flavour of the cream.

practice.prompt: In 'un mur de pierre', does de introduce the wall's material or something poured into it?
practice.explanation: De can introduce material in an established noun group; it does not always mean contents.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual transport preposition: 'Je voyage ___ avion.'
practice.explanation: Air travel is en avion.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: 'Nous allons ___ pied.'
practice.explanation: The fixed expression is à pied.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition naming contents: 'une tasse ___ thé'.
practice.explanation: De introduces the contents.

practice.prompt: Supply the infinitive from laver: 'une machine à ___'.
practice.explanation: A function after à uses an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply the mode preposition: 'Elle vient ___ voiture.'
practice.explanation: The ordinary expression is en voiture, without an article.

practice.prompt: Supply the reference preposition for horseback travel: 'Il part ___ cheval.'
practice.explanation: The conventional expression is à cheval.

practice.prompt: You are inside a bus, not on its roof. Supply dans or sur: 'Je suis ___ le bus.'
practice.explanation: French uses dans le bus for the ordinary interior location.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual street-activity preposition: 'Nous marchons ___ la rue.'
practice.explanation: The ordinary general expression is dans la rue.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition for material: 'une chaise ___ bois'.
practice.explanation: En introduces the material.

practice.prompt: Name an empty cup intended for coffee: 'une tasse ___ café'.
practice.explanation: À names the intended type or function.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition in the established compound: 'une brosse ___ dents'.
practice.explanation: The toothbrush compound is une brosse à dents.

practice.prompt: Supply the full infinitive after à: 'une salle à ___' means a dining room. Use manger.
practice.explanation: The verb naming the room's function stays infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply en or dans: 'Je voyage ___ train, mais maintenant je suis dans la gare.'
practice.explanation: En train names the travel mode.

practice.prompt: Supply de with elision for contents: 'un verre ___ eau'.
practice.explanation: De elides before eau.

practice.prompt: Rewrite the whole phrase, changing only the verb to its required form: 'une machine à coud'.
practice.explanation: The noun's function is named with an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Which phrase describes a travel mode rather than a physical position?
practice.explanation: En métro means by metro; dans le métro locates someone inside the system or vehicle.

production_task.prompt: Describe your trip to a shop and an object you need there. Include a travel mode, an interior or street location and a noun group with `à` or `en`.
production_task.model_answer: Je vais au magasin en bus. Dans le bus, je lis ma liste. J'ai besoin d'une brosse à dents.
production_task.translation: I am going to the shop by bus. On the bus, I read my list. I need a toothbrush.
rubric: Keep the preposition in the compound noun.
Do not conjugate a functional infinitive if you use one.
